problem: A logistics company is testing a new drone delivery protocol using moving trains. At exactly 12:00 PM, a heavily loaded freight train departs from Central Station, traveling east along a straight track at a constant speed of 40 miles per hour. Exactly two hours later, at 2:00 PM, an express passenger train departs from Central Station on a parallel track, also traveling east, but at a constant speed of 60 miles per hour. At the exact moment the passenger train departs (2:00 PM), a high-speed drone launches from the front of the passenger train. The drone flies directly east towards the freight train at a constant speed of 120 miles per hour. As soon as the drone reaches the freight train, it instantaneously reverses direction and flies back to the passenger train at the exact same speed. It continues flying back and forth between the two moving trains without losing any time or speed during the turns. The drone continues this continuous zigzag flight pattern until the exact moment the passenger train catches up to and is side-by-side with the freight train. Calculate the total distance, in miles, that the freight train traveled strictly during the time the drone was actively flying.
